## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

The *Revatīpetavatthu* (Pv 39) is a narrative poem preserved in the *Petavatthu* of the Khuddaka Nikāya. In this text, two hell wardens confront the deceased Revatī, explaining the karmic retribution resulting from her evil deeds on earth and contrasting her plight with the heavenly rewards gained through the religious merit of her husband.

 Furthermore, Revatī or her story is cross-referenced in numerous canonical and paracanonical contexts, including several suttas of the *Vimānavatthu* (such as Vv 15, Vv 19, Vv 22–25, and Vv 37), the *Surucijātaka* (Ja 489), the *Mittātherīgāthā* (Thig 2.7), the *Catumahārājasutta* and *Dutiyacatumahārājasutta* (AN 3.37, AN 3.38), and the *Sānusutta* (SN 10.5).
